question: Which of the following towns was grown as a temple town during the Chola dynasty?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Bhillasvamin.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A "temple town" is an urban centre that grew around a large temple, which acted as the focus of economic activity, drawing devotees, priests, artisans and traders to the site. (मंदिर नगर — भिल्लस्वामिन)

 

• Bhillasvamin (present-day Bhilsa/Vidisha in Madhya Pradesh) is cited as one of the early towns that developed around an important temple site, a process of temple-centred urbanisation that intensified across India, including under the patronage of royal dynasties such as the Cholas of south India.

 

• Chola rulers like Rajaraja I and Rajendra I were prolific temple builders who endowed temples with land grants (*devadana*/*brahmadeya*), turning temple precincts into hubs of pilgrimage, craft production and trade — the same pattern of growth associated with towns like Bhillasvamin.

 

• Other well-known temple towns of the Chola period include Thanjavur, Kumbakonam and Chidambaram, the site of the magnificent Brihadishvara Temple built by Rajaraja I.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Brihadishvara Temple at Thanjavur, built in the early 11th century CE, is a UNESCO World Heritage Site and one of the largest temples in India.

 

• Land grants (devadana/brahmadeya) made temples major landowners and employers, accelerating the growth of towns around them.

 

NOTE

 

• Ajmer (Option 2): Grew in prominence under the Chauhan (Chahamana) dynasty and later the Mughals; it is associated with the Dargah of Khwaja Moinuddin Chishti, not the Cholas.

 

• Ahmedabad (Option 3): Founded in 1411 CE by Sultan Ahmed Shah I of the Gujarat Sultanate; unconnected to the Chola dynasty.

 

• Ahmednagar (Option 4): Founded in 1490 CE by Ahmad Nizam Shah I, founder of the Ahmadnagar Sultanate in the Deccan; unconnected to the Chola dynasty.

question: The major resources of Gondwana coal, which are metallurgical coal are located in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Damadar valley.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gondwana coal fields, of Permian age, hold over 98% of India's total coal reserves and are found across peninsular India. (गोंडवाना कोयला — दामोदर घाटी)

 

• The best-quality metallurgical (coking) coal deposits of the Gondwana system are concentrated in the Damodar Valley, spread across Jharkhand and West Bengal, including the famous Jharia and Raniganj coalfields.

 

• Jharia holds India's largest reserves of coking coal and is critical to the steel industry, supplying raw material to plants such as Jamshedpur, Bokaro and Durgapur.

 

• Because of its dense concentration of coal mines and heavy industry, the Damodar Valley is often called the "Ruhr of India", after Germany's industrial Ruhr region.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other major Gondwana coalfields — Talcher and IB River Valley (Odisha), Singrauli (MP/UP), Korba (Chhattisgarh), Godavari Valley (Telangana/Andhra Pradesh) — mostly yield non-coking (thermal) coal.

 

• The Damodar Valley Corporation (DVC), set up in 1948, was modelled on the USA's Tennessee Valley Authority for multipurpose river-valley development.

 

NOTE

 

• Chambal valley (Option 2): Known for the Chambal ravines and the Gandhi Sagar, Rana Pratap Sagar and Jawahar Sagar dams; not a coal-bearing tract.

 

• Krishna valley (Option 3): Important for irrigation and hydel projects in the Deccan; has negligible coal reserves.

 

• Narmada valley (Option 4): Known for the Sardar Sarovar and Indira Sagar projects; not a significant coal-producing belt.

question: The ICC Women's cricket World Cup 2022 was held in _________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is New Zealand.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 2022 ICC Women's Cricket World Cup, the 12th edition of the tournament, was hosted by New Zealand from 4 March to 3 April 2022. (महिला क्रिकेट विश्व कप 2022 — न्यूज़ीलैंड)

 

• Australia won the tournament, defeating England in the final held at Hagley Oval, Christchurch, to claim their 7th Women's World Cup title.

 

• Player of the Match in the final, Alyssa Healy (Australia), scored a match-winning century.

 

• India, captained by Mithali Raj, was knocked out in the league stage and did not reach the semi-finals in this edition.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• New Zealand had earlier hosted the Women's World Cup in 2000 as well.

 

• The 2025 edition of the ICC Women's Cricket World Cup was hosted by India, with Australia again emerging champions.

 

NOTE

 

• England (Option 1): Hosted the previous edition of the Women's World Cup in 2017, and were runners-up in the 2022 edition; they did not host the 2022 tournament.

 

• India (Option 2): Participated in the 2022 edition but did not host it; India hosted the subsequent 2025 edition.

 

• Australia (Option 3): Won the 2022 tournament as a participant but the event was not held on Australian soil.

question: Identify an example of organisms that do NOT belong to the third trophic level.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Cows.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A trophic level is a step in a food chain: producers occupy the first level, primary consumers (herbivores) the second, secondary consumers (carnivores that eat herbivores) the third, and so on. (पोषण स्तर — तृतीय पोषण स्तर)

 

• Cows are pure herbivores that feed directly on plants (producers); hence they occupy the second trophic level (primary consumers), not the third.

 

• Fishes, Wolves and Birds, when they prey on herbivorous animals such as smaller fish, insects or rodents, act as secondary consumers (carnivores) and thus fall in the third trophic level.

 

• Of the four options, only the cow, being a strict herbivore, fails to fit the third trophic level.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The fourth trophic level and beyond is occupied by top/apex carnivores such as tigers, lions and eagles.

 

• Energy transfer between successive trophic levels follows the 10% Law, proposed by Raymond Lindeman.

 

NOTE

 

• Fishes (Option 1): Many fish species are carnivorous, preying on smaller fish or zooplankton, placing them at the third trophic level.

 

• Wolves (Option 2): Wolves are carnivores that prey on herbivores like deer, making them third-trophic-level consumers.

 

• Birds (Option 3): Many birds (insectivorous or piscivorous) prey on primary consumers, placing them at the third trophic level.

question: In 'Andes Mountain' of South America animal which is used for transportation is ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Llamas.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Llama is a domesticated South American camelid traditionally used by the indigenous people of the Andes Mountains as a pack animal, valued for its ability to carry loads at high altitude. (लामा — एंडीज पर्वत)

 

• Llamas, along with related camelids such as alpacas, vicuñas and guanacos, are well adapted to the cold, thin-air conditions of the high Andes.

 

• Andean communities across Peru, Bolivia, Ecuador and Chile have used llamas for centuries to transport goods across mountainous terrain, as well as for wool, meat and hide.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The alpaca, a smaller camelid, is prized chiefly for its fine wool rather than as a pack animal.

 

• The guanaco and vicuña are the wild ancestral relatives of the llama and alpaca respectively.

 

NOTE

 

• Bullocks (Option 1): Used for transport and ploughing mainly in the Indian subcontinent and other agrarian plains, not specifically the Andes.

 

• Camels (Option 2): The traditional transport animal of hot deserts such as the Sahara and Thar, not the Andes.

 

• Donkeys (Option 3): Widely used as pack animals worldwide but are not the animal specifically associated with Andean transport; that role belongs to the native llama.

question: The early Turkish rulers ruled between _____ years over Delhi.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1206 and 1290.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The early Turkish rulers of Delhi, commonly known as the Slave (Mamluk/Ilbari) Dynasty, ruled from 1206 to 1290 CE. (गुलाम वंश — 1206 से 1290)

 

• The dynasty was founded by Qutb-ud-din Aibak in 1206, following the death of Muhammad of Ghor.

 

• It came to an end in 1290 when Jalaluddin Khalji overthrew the last Mamluk ruler, Shamsuddin Kayumars, and established the Khalji dynasty.

 

• Notable rulers of this dynasty include Iltutmish, Raziyya Sultana (India's first woman monarch) and Ghiyasuddin Balban.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Qutub Minar in Delhi was started by Qutb-ud-din Aibak and completed by his successor Iltutmish.

 

• Balban is known for his "Theory of Kingship" and the introduction of strict court ceremonials like *sijda* and *paibos*.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 give date ranges that do not correspond to any recognised span of the early Turkish (Slave dynasty) rule over Delhi, which is historically fixed at 1206–1290.

question: Surekha Punekar is a __________ dancer from the Indian state of Maharashtra.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lavani.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Surekha Punekar is a well-known exponent of Lavani, a traditional dance-and-song form of Maharashtra performed predominantly by women. (लावणी — सुरेखा पुनेकर)

 

• She has performed and popularised Lavani widely, including internationally, and has trained numerous students in the art form through her dance academy.

 

• Lavani is traditionally accompanied by the dholki and is marked by powerful rhythm and expressive body movements; historically it was performed to entertain soldiers and also to convey social and political satire.

 

• Lavani has two broad forms — Phadachi Lavani (performed on a public stage) and Baithakichi Lavani (performed in a seated, intimate setting).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Tamasha is the broader folk theatre tradition of Maharashtra within which Lavani performances are often embedded.

 

• Lavani gained wider recognition through Marathi cinema and has been showcased on national platforms as a symbol of Maharashtrian folk culture.

 

NOTE

 

• Tamasha (Option 1): A folk theatre form of Maharashtra combining dance, music, and drama, not a solo dance style.

 

• Povada (Option 3): A ballad-singing tradition of Maharashtra that celebrates heroic deeds, especially of Chhatrapati Shivaji Maharaj.

 

• Koli (Option 4): A folk dance performed by the fisherfolk (Koli community) of Maharashtra, depicting activities like rowing and fishing.

question: The 15th Men's FIH hockey World Cup will be held in the year ________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2023.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The 15th Men's FIH Hockey World Cup was held in 2023 in India, at Bhubaneswar and Rourkela, Odisha (Kalinga Stadium and Birsa Munda International Hockey Stadium). (हॉकी विश्व कप — 2023, भारत)

 

• Germany won the tournament, defeating Belgium in the final.

 

• This was the second consecutive time India hosted the men's Hockey World Cup, having previously hosted the 2018 edition at Bhubaneswar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's men's hockey team finished 9th at the 2023 World Cup, with New Zealand defeating them in the classification match.

 

• The Kalinga Stadium, Bhubaneswar, has become a regular venue for major international hockey events in India.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (2022, 2025 and 2024) do not correspond to the actual hosting year of the 15th Men's FIH Hockey World Cup, which was 2023.

question: The core of earth is made up of ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is nickel and iron.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Earth's core, comprising an inner core and an outer core, is primarily composed of iron and nickel, often referred to by the abbreviation NiFe. (पृथ्वी की क्रोड — निकल और लोहा)

 

• The inner core is solid, despite extremely high temperatures, because of the immense pressure at that depth (about 5,150–6,371 km).

 

• The outer core is liquid, and its convective motion, combined with Earth's rotation, generates the planet's magnetic field through the geodynamo process.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The layer above the core, the mantle, is composed mainly of silicate rocks rich in iron and magnesium.

 

• The Earth's crust, the outermost solid layer, is dominated by lighter elements like oxygen, silicon and aluminium.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 3 (cobalt/nickel, iron/cobalt, nickel/magnesium) misidentify the core's composition; cobalt and magnesium are not the principal core-forming elements.

question: Who among the following is NOT an exponent of Mohiniyattam classical dance form?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Prateeksha Kashi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mohiniyattam is a classical dance form of Kerala, known as the "dance of the enchantress" for its graceful, swaying movements. (मोहिनीअट्टम — प्रतीक्षा काशी कुचिपुड़ी नृत्यांगना)

 

• Prateeksha Kashi is a noted exponent, choreographer and teacher of Kuchipudi, not Mohiniyattam, and runs a dance institution in Bengaluru.

 

• Smitha Rajan and Jayaprabha Menon are recognised Mohiniyattam performers; Jayaprabha Menon in particular heads the International Academy of Mohiniyattam.

 

• Radha Dutta is credited with introducing formal Mohiniyattam training in the Washington, D.C. area of the USA.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kalamandalam Kalyanikutty Amma is credited with reviving and systematising Mohiniyattam in the 20th century.

 

• Mohiniyattam is traditionally a solo dance performed by women, accompanied by Carnatic music.

 

NOTE

 

• Smitha Rajan (Option 1), Jayaprabha Menon (Option 2) and Radha Dutta (Option 4) are all genuine, recognised exponents of Mohiniyattam, so they are eliminated as the odd one out.

question: Fundamental Rights are mentioned in which part of the Constitution of India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Part III.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fundamental Rights are enshrined in Part III of the Constitution of India, spanning Articles 12 to 35. (मूल अधिकार — भाग III)

 

• Part III is often described as the "Magna Carta" of the Indian Constitution and is directly enforceable by courts under Article 32 (Right to Constitutional Remedies).

 

• The Fundamental Rights originally numbered seven; the Right to Property was removed from this list by the 44th Constitutional Amendment Act, 1978, leaving six categories today (Right to Equality, Right to Freedom, Right against Exploitation, Right to Freedom of Religion, Cultural and Educational Rights, and Right to Constitutional Remedies).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Part IV of the Constitution contains the Directive Principles of State Policy (Articles 36–51), which are non-justiciable.

 

• Part IVA (Article 51A) contains the Fundamental Duties, added by the 42nd Amendment Act, 1976.

 

NOTE

 

• Part IV (Option 1): Deals with the Directive Principles of State Policy, not Fundamental Rights.

 

• Part VI (Option 3): Deals with the structure and functioning of State Governments.

 

• Part IX (Option 4): Deals with Panchayats (local self-government in rural areas).

question: The famous hill station udagamandalam is also known as ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ooty.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Udhagamandalam is the official/local Tamil name of the popular hill station commonly known as Ooty (Ootacamund). (ऊटी — उदगमंडलम)

 

• It is situated in the Nilgiris district of Tamil Nadu, at an elevation of about 2,240 metres, in the Nilgiri hill range of the Western Ghats.

 

• Ooty is a well-known tourist destination, famous for its tea gardens, the Government Botanical Garden, and the UNESCO-listed Nilgiri Mountain Railway.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Nilgiri Mountain Railway, a UNESCO World Heritage Site, connects Mettupalayam to Ooty via Coonoor.

 

• Ooty served as the summer capital of the erstwhile Madras Presidency during British rule.

 

NOTE

 

• Kodaikanal (Option 1): A hill station in the Palani Hills of Tamil Nadu, distinct from Ooty.

 

• Shivpuri (Option 2): A city/former hill retreat in Madhya Pradesh, unrelated to Ooty.

 

• Mussoorie (Option 4): A hill station in Uttarakhand, in the Himalayan foothills, unrelated to Ooty.

question: The Council of Ministers shall not exceed ___% of the total number of members of the Assembly of States.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 15.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Under Article 164(1A) of the Constitution, inserted by the 91st Constitutional Amendment Act, 2003, the total number of Ministers, including the Chief Minister, in a State's Council of Ministers shall not exceed 15% of the total number of members of the Legislative Assembly of that State. (मंत्रिपरिषद — विधानसभा सदस्यों का 15%)

 

• The same amendment also fixed a minimum of 12 Ministers for smaller states/UTs, so that the Council of Ministers is neither too large nor too small.

 

• A parallel provision, Article 75(1A), caps the size of the Union Council of Ministers at 15% of the total strength of the Lok Sabha.

 

• The 91st Amendment was enacted to curb the practice of oversized ministries formed to accommodate coalition partners.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 91st Amendment Act, 2003 also added the anti-defection strengthening provisions, barring disqualified members from holding ministerial or other remunerative political posts.

 

• Before this amendment, there was no constitutional cap on the size of the Council of Ministers at the Union or State level.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (20%, 12% and 10%) do not match the constitutionally fixed ceiling of 15% under Articles 75(1A) and 164(1A).

question: The United Nations Environment Programme has signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the _______ government to support its 'Majhi Vasundhara' campaign.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Maharashtra.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• 'Majhi Vasundhara' ("My Earth") is an environmental campaign launched by the Government of Maharashtra (Environment and Climate Change Department) to promote sustainability across five elements — earth, water, air, fire and sky (Panchtatva). (माझी वसुंधरा — महाराष्ट्र सरकार)

 

• The campaign encourages urban local bodies, gram panchayats and citizens across Maharashtra to take up climate action and green initiatives, with performance-based recognition/awards.

 

• The United Nations Environment Programme (UNEP) signed a Memorandum of Understanding with the Maharashtra government to lend technical support to this campaign.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Maharashtra's Majhi Vasundhara campaign was first launched in 2020 and has since progressed through successive editions.

 

• UNEP is headquartered in Nairobi, Kenya, and works globally on environmental sustainability initiatives.

 

NOTE

 

• Rajasthan (Option 2), Karnataka (Option 3) and Gujarat (Option 4): None of these state governments run the 'Majhi Vasundhara' campaign — it is specific to Maharashtra, and UNEP's MoU on this campaign was signed with the Maharashtra government.

question: Among the following, which contains the lowest amount of sugar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Potato.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Among common fruits and vegetables, the potato contains the lowest amount of sugar — its carbohydrate content is mostly in the form of starch, not free sugars. (आलू — सबसे कम शर्करा)

 

• Fruits such as apple, mango and banana naturally contain higher levels of simple sugars (fructose, glucose, sucrose), giving them their characteristic sweetness.

 

• Approximate sugar content per 100g: potato (~0.8g), apple (~10g), banana (~12g), mango (~14g) — potato is far lower than all three fruits.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Potato is classified botanically as a tuber/vegetable, not a fruit, which is one reason its sugar profile differs sharply from that of apples, mangoes and bananas.

 

• Among the fruits listed, mango generally has the highest sugar content, followed by banana and then apple.

 

NOTE

 

• Apple (Option 1), Mango (Option 2) and Banana (Option 4): All are fruits with comparatively high natural sugar content, and hence rank above potato, not below it.

question:
The Family Courts (Amendment) Bill was introduced in Lok Sabha on July 18, 2022.

Under this act, which of the following states has set up Family Courts?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Family Courts (Amendment) Bill, 2022 was introduced in the Lok Sabha on 18 July 2022 to give retrospective statutory validity to family courts already functioning in certain states without formal Central Government notification under the Family Courts Act, 1984. (कौटुंबिक न्यायालय संशोधन विधेयक — हिमाचल प्रदेश)

 

• The Bill specifically validated the establishment of family courts in Himachal Pradesh (set up in 2019) and Nagaland, ensuring that orders passed by these courts were not rendered invalid on technical grounds.

 

• The Family Courts Act, 1984 empowers state governments, in consultation with the High Court, to establish Family Courts for the resolution of family disputes such as divorce, maintenance and child custody.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Family Courts aim to promote conciliation and speedy settlement of disputes relating to marriage and family affairs, and follow simplified rules of evidence and procedure.

 

• The amendment Bill was passed by Parliament in 2022 to remove legal ambiguity around the validity of orders passed by the affected family courts.

 

NOTE

 

• Arunachal Pradesh (Option 2), Assam (Option 3) and Gujarat (Option 4): These states were not the ones whose family courts required retrospective validation under the 2022 Amendment Bill — that validation applied specifically to Himachal Pradesh and Nagaland.

question: Which of the following organisations of the Government of India has been reporting the GDP at factor cost and at market prices?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Central Statistics Office.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Central Statistics Office (CSO), functioning under the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), has been the body responsible for compiling and reporting India's National Accounts Statistics, including GDP at factor cost and GDP at market prices. (केंद्रीय सांख्यिकी कार्यालय — जीडीपी)

 

• The CSO releases estimates such as Gross Domestic Product (GDP), Gross Value Added (GVA) and Net National Income (NNI) at both factor cost and market prices, along with growth rate projections (advance, provisional and final estimates).

 

• In 2019, the CSO was merged with the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO) to form the National Statistical Office (NSO), which now continues this function under MoSPI.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• GDP at factor cost measures output based on the cost of production (excluding taxes, including subsidies), while GDP at market prices includes indirect taxes and excludes subsidies.

 

• MoSPI also releases the Index of Industrial Production (IIP) and Consumer Price Index (CPI) data through its various wings.

 

NOTE

 

• Reserve Bank of India (Option 1): India's central bank, responsible for monetary policy and currency management, not for compiling GDP estimates.

 

• National Sample Survey Organisation (Option 2): Conducted large-scale sample surveys (e.g., on employment, consumption); it did not itself compile the official GDP figures, which was the CSO's mandate.

 

• NITI Aayog (Option 4): A policy think tank that uses GDP data for planning purposes but does not compile or release the official GDP estimates.

question: Who founded the value of 'G'?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Henry Cavendish.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Henry Cavendish, a British scientist, conducted the famous Cavendish Experiment in 1798 using a torsion balance to measure the density of the Earth, from which the value of the universal gravitational constant (G) could subsequently be derived. (गुरुत्वाकर्षण स्थिरांक — हेनरी कैवेंडिश)

 

• The currently accepted value of G is approximately 6.674 × 10⁻¹¹ N·m²/kg².

 

• Cavendish's experiment is widely regarded as one of the earliest precise measurements in experimental physics and is sometimes called "weighing the Earth".

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Isaac Newton formulated the Universal Law of Gravitation (F = Gm₁m₂/r²) roughly a century before Cavendish's experiment, but he did not experimentally determine the numerical value of G.

 

• Cavendish's original goal was to determine the mean density of the Earth, not G directly — the value of G was calculated from his results afterward.

 

NOTE

 

• Michael Faraday (Option 2): Known for his pioneering work on electromagnetic induction, unrelated to determining G.

 

• Isaac Newton (Option 3): Formulated the theory/law of gravitation but did not experimentally measure the value of G.

 

• Marie Curie (Option 4): Known for her research on radioactivity and the discovery of polonium and radium, unrelated to G.

question: Which Indian musician served as the artistic director of the World Music Department at the Rotterdam Music Conservatory in the Netherlands?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hariprasad Chaurasia.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Hariprasad Chaurasia, the renowned Indian bansuri (bamboo flute) maestro, served as the artistic director of the World Music Department at the Rotterdam Music Conservatory in the Netherlands. (पंडित हरिप्रसाद चौरसिया — रॉटरडैम म्यूजिक कंज़र्वेटरी)

 

• He is a recipient of India's highest civilian and artistic honours, including the Padma Vibhushan and the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award.

 

• Chaurasia has also founded institutions to train students in classical bansuri music, including the Vrindavan Gurukul in Mumbai (2006) and Bhubaneswar (2010).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Hariprasad Chaurasia has collaborated extensively with international musicians and composed music for numerous Hindi films, including alongside Shivkumar Sharma as the duo Shiv-Hari.

 

• The Rotterdam Music Conservatory (Codarts) is known for its World Music programme that brings together musicians from diverse global traditions.

 

NOTE

 

• Pravin Godkhindi (Option 2): A noted Indian flautist known for Hindustani and fusion music, but not associated with this Rotterdam role.

 

• Ronu Majumdar (Option 3): A well-known bansuri player of the Maihar-Senia gharana, but not the artistic director referred to here.

 

• Nityanand Haldipur (Option 4): A respected Hindustani classical flautist, but not associated with the Rotterdam Music Conservatory's World Music Department.

question: Identify the statement that is NOT true about ATP.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Secretion of enzymes.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• ATP (Adenosine Triphosphate) is known as the "energy currency of the cell", supplying energy for numerous vital biochemical processes. (एटीपी — कोशिका की ऊर्जा मुद्रा)

 

• ATP directly powers muscle contraction (sliding of actin-myosin filaments), nerve impulse propagation (maintaining ion gradients via the sodium-potassium pump) and protein synthesis (formation of peptide bonds during translation).

 

• Secretion of enzymes, however, is primarily a process of synthesis and release via the endoplasmic reticulum-Golgi pathway and exocytosis; it is not one of ATP's classically listed direct physiological roles in the way the other three options are.

 

• Hence, of the four statements, "secretion of enzymes" is identified as the one that is NOT a recognised direct function of ATP in this context.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• ATP is produced mainly through cellular respiration (glycolysis, Krebs cycle and oxidative phosphorylation) occurring in the mitochondria.

 

• ATP consists of adenine, ribose sugar, and three phosphate groups; energy is released when the terminal phosphate bond is hydrolysed, converting ATP to ADP.

 

NOTE

 

• Nerve impulse propagation (Option 1), Contraction of muscles (Option 3) and Protein synthesis (Option 4): All three are well-established, energy-demanding processes directly powered by ATP, and are therefore eliminated as the statement being asked for.

question: The Industrial Policy Resolution 1956, classified industries into how many categories?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Industrial Policy Resolution (IPR), 1956, adopted under Jawaharlal Nehru, classified industries into three categories (Schedules A, B and C) based on the roles of the public and private sectors. (औद्योगिक नीति संकल्प 1956 — तीन श्रेणियां)

 

• Schedule A comprised industries reserved exclusively for the public sector (e.g., defence, atomic energy, railways).

 

• Schedule B comprised industries in which the state would increasingly set up new units, while private enterprise was expected to supplement state efforts.

 

• Schedule C comprised the remaining industries left to the private sector, though still subject to overall government regulation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The IPR 1956 is often referred to as the "Economic Constitution of India" because it laid the framework for industrial development in the mixed-economy model.

 

• It followed the earlier Industrial Policy Resolution of 1948, which had first outlined the broad role of the state versus private enterprise after Independence.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (5, 6 and 4 categories) do not match the well-established three-fold Schedule A/B/C classification introduced by the IPR, 1956.

question: The iron pillar situated at Mehrauli, Delhi is belonged to which of the following Gupta ruler?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Chandragupta II.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Iron Pillar at Mehrauli, Delhi, bears a Sanskrit inscription referring to a king named "Chandra", who is widely identified by historians as the Gupta emperor Chandragupta II (Vikramaditya). (मेहरौली लौह स्तंभ — चंद्रगुप्त द्वितीय)

 

• The pillar, made of nearly rust-free wrought iron, stands about 7.2 metres tall and is renowned for its remarkable metallurgical corrosion resistance, having stood for over 1,600 years.

 

• Chandragupta II ruled the Gupta Empire during its golden age (c. 375–415 CE), expanding the empire and adopting the title Vikramaditya.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Iron Pillar was originally believed to have been erected at Udayagiri (Madhya Pradesh) and later relocated to its present site near the Qutub Minar complex in Delhi.

 

• Chandragupta II's court is traditionally associated with the "Navaratnas" (nine gems), including the poet Kalidasa, though this association is debated among historians.

 

NOTE

 

• Skandagupta (Option 1): Known for repelling the Huna invasions, but not associated with the Mehrauli Iron Pillar.

 

• Samudragupta (Option 2): Known as the "Napoleon of India" for his military conquests, commemorated mainly through the Allahabad Prashasti (Prayag Prashasti), not the Iron Pillar.

 

• Kumaragupta (Option 3): Founder of Nalanda University, but not linked to the Mehrauli Iron Pillar inscription.

question: Vasco da Gama, a Portuguese explorer, discovered the sea route to India in ______.
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1498.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vasco da Gama, a Portuguese explorer, discovered the sea route from Europe to India by sailing around the Cape of Good Hope, arriving at Calicut (Kozhikode), Kerala, on 20 May 1498. (वास्को द गामा — 1498, कालीकट)

 

• This voyage established the first direct maritime trade link between Europe and India, breaking the Arab-Venetian monopoly over the spice trade.

 

• Da Gama was received by the Zamorin of Calicut, and his arrival paved the way for extensive Portuguese trading presence and eventual colonial expansion in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Bartolomeu Dias, another Portuguese explorer, was the first European to round the Cape of Good Hope in 1488, paving the way for da Gama's later voyage.

 

• The Portuguese later established their first Indian settlement/colony at Goa in 1510, under Afonso de Albuquerque.

 

NOTE

 

• 1488 (Option 1): The year Bartolomeu Dias rounded the Cape of Good Hope, not the year da Gama reached India.

 

• 1508 and 1518 (Options 3 and 4): Do not correspond to Vasco da Gama's historic voyage; India had already been reached a decade earlier, in 1498.

question: Name the classical dancer who was given the Prani Mitra Award in 1968.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rukmini Devi Arundale.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale, the eminent Bharatanatyam dancer, theosophist and founder of Kalakshetra, was conferred the "Prani Mitra" Award in 1968, which recognises outstanding contribution to animal welfare. (प्राणी मित्र पुरस्कार — रुक्मिणी देवी अरुंडेल)

 

• Besides her contributions to reviving Bharatanatyam from its temple-dance origins, she was a lifelong animal welfare activist, and served as founder-chairperson of the Animal Welfare Board of India.

 

• She was also the first woman nominated to the Rajya Sabha, and was honoured with the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award and the Padma Bhushan.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Rukmini Devi Arundale founded Kalakshetra, a premier institution for Bharatanatyam and other Indian classical arts, in Chennai in 1936.

 

• She reportedly declined the offer to become the President of India in 1977, preferring to continue her work in the arts and animal welfare.

 

NOTE

 

• Dr Padma Subrahmanyam (Option 1): A renowned Bharatanatyam exponent and scholar known for developing the Karanas based on the Natya Shastra, but not the recipient of the 1968 Prani Mitra Award.

 

• Shovana Narayan (Option 2): A celebrated Kathak dancer, unrelated to this award.

 

• Bipin Singh (Option 4): Credited with reviving and popularising Manipuri dance in mainland India, but not associated with the 1968 Prani Mitra Award.

question: In August 2022, the Union government has appointed _______as a director in the Prime Minister's Office (PMO).
solution_text:
The correct answer is Shweta Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• In August 2022, the Union government appointed Shweta Singh, an officer of the Indian Foreign Service (IFS), as a Director in the Prime Minister's Office (PMO). (प्रधानमंत्री कार्यालय — श्वेता सिंह)

 

• Prior to this appointment, Shweta Singh had served in various diplomatic and administrative capacities within the Indian Foreign Service.

 

• Directors in the PMO assist in coordinating policy matters and liaison between the Prime Minister's Office and various ministries/departments of the Union government.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The PMO functions under the direct charge of the Prime Minister and comprises officers drawn from the IAS, IFS, IPS and other government services, headed by the Principal Secretary to the Prime Minister.

 

• The PMO plays a key coordinating role across ministries on policy formulation, monitoring of programmes and international engagements.

 

NOTE

 

• Gopal Vittal (Option 1): A corporate executive, CEO of Bharti Airtel, unrelated to this PMO appointment.

 

• Rajesh Verma (Option 2): An IAS officer who has served as Union Cabinet Secretary and in other senior administrative roles, but not the officer appointed as Director, PMO, in August 2022 referred to here.

 

• Anuj Poddar (Option 3): A corporate executive associated with the private sector, unrelated to this PMO appointment.
